resources.name: Contact Congress (Open Source)
resources.desc: Send emails to members of the US Congress. This was developed by EFF as an open source project. They use it for their own campaigns internally. There is also a hosted version run by Fight for the Future (see below).

resources.name: Call Congress
resources.desc: Coordinate call-in days to US Congress, the President, or local or corporate targets. Original project from Fight for the Future and Taskforce.is, but with lots of development from Mozilla and the EFF. Frontend looks like this, https://call.mozilla.org and the backend looks like http://callpower.org. A hosted version is available, and the code is AGPL.

resources.name: Twilio.org's Rapid Response Kit
resources.desc: Collection phone-related tools using Twilio's service. Kit includes: Auto-Respond (inbound voice/sms responder), Broadcast (simple way to broadcast texts/calls to a list), Conference Line, Forwarder, Ringdown (call down a list of people, if 1st person doesn't answer go on to the next), Help Line (Press 1 for..., Press 2 for...)

resources.name: Ushahidi
resources.desc: Platform for data management and visualization. Other tools include CrowdMap, CrisisNET (data about world crises), Ping (tool for checking is someone is ok after an emergency), SMSsync (two-way SMS gateway). Check out their github repos.

resources.name: Crowdring
resources.desc: web app where people around the world can place a free missed call to sign a petition

resources.name: Self Starter
resources.desc: roll your own crowdfunding site

resources.name: TakeCharge.io
resources.desc: opensource or SaaS online donations powered by Stripe.

resources.name: Countdown
resources.desc: A quick & simple tool for making your own webpage with a countdown to your upcoming event.

resources.name: CiviCRM
resources.desc: Contact management system for non-profit / activist sector, including donations, memberships, events, SMS, bulk mail & full CRM.

resources.name: Spoke
resources.desc: Text-distribution tool for organizations to mobilize supporters and members into action. Spoke allows you to upload phone numbers, customize scripts and assign volunteers to communicate with supporters while allowing organizations to manage the process.

resources.name: Loomio
resources.desc: Tool for collaborative decision-making in groups. Note: Loomio's code is also open source, but it's generally used as a hosted service.

resources.name: Contact Congress (FFTF)
resources.desc: Used to send emails to members of the US Congress. This is Fight for the Future's hosted-version of the open sources Contact Congress. Ideal for organizations that send a lot of emails to congress, but who don't have tech staff who can install and maintain their own version of the open source software.

resources.name: ControlShift
resources.desc: Distributed petitions, events and local groups for progressive advocacy organizations. Tools to help make campaigns more participatory.

resources.name: Riseup
resources.desc: A provider of communication tools for activists, including free webmail, chat, and VPN

resources.name: Action Network
resources.desc: A nonprofit digital organizing toolset for progressive organizations. Includes petitions, advocacy, fundraising, mass email, and more for free or cheap.

resources.name: MoveOn's Petition Platform
resources.desc: Start your own petition on MoveOn's hosted platform. If your petition gains traction, MoveOn staff may help support you.

resources.name: CiviWiki
resources.desc: An open-source, non-profit community, working to develop a democratic engagement web system.

resources.name: Tails
resources.desc: A live media, Linux-based operating system that is designed to allow the use of a computer without leaving a digital footprint.

resources.name: Tor Browser
resources.desc: Free software for enabling anonymous communication. It prevents somebody watching your Internet connection from learning what sites you visit, it prevents the sites you visit from learning your physical location, and it lets you access sites which are blocked.

resources.name: Brave Browser
resources.desc: Brave is a free and open-source web browser developed by Brave Software, Inc. based on the Chromium web browser. It blocks ads and website trackers, and provides a way for users to send information contributions in the form of Basic Attention Tokens to websites and content creators.

resources.name: Where@
resources.desc: a mobile app to help protesters communicate with each other in realtime during marches

resources.name: Day of Action
resources.desc: very rough tool used to coordinate a day of action for high school students. the starting point for a more generalized tool to run a day of action campaign
resources.section: Projects to keep an eye on (ie projects in development)

resources.name: Umbrella App
resources.desc: an open source Android App with lessons and checklists on digital and physical security topics ranging from sending a secure mail to dealing with physical surveillance and attending a protest safely. Also includes forms for responding to security incidents and feeds to ensure users are up to date with the latest security information for their area. Also available in Spanish and Chinese.

resources.name: Code Corps
resources.desc: code corps hopes to provide tools that connect people to projects that have a social impact, facilitate crowdfunding, and provide support for those working on projects

resources.name: Thunderclap
resources.desc: use this to coordinate a group sharing the same message on social media at the same time. You write a tweet, make a campaign, and ask people to pledge to support your campaign. When you reach your goal of a certain number of pledgers, your tweet will automatically be posted to each pledger's social media.
